questions.question: Kojagiri Poornima is a festival celebrated primarily in _______ on the full moon day of Ashwin month.

questions.question: Which of the following States/Union Territories of India receives the highest average annual rainfall?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya** receives the highest average annual rainfall in India.
 
• It is home to Mawsynram, which holds the record for being the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of about 11,871 millimeters.
 
• The heavy rainfall in Meghalaya is primarily due to its geographic location, being situated in the windward side of the Khasi Hills, which traps moisture-laden monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The region's unique topography and climate contribute to its high levels of precipitation, supporting lush greenery and diverse ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi** receives an average annual rainfall of around 800 millimeters, primarily during the monsoon season.
 
• **Ladakh** is a cold desert and receives very little rainfall, averaging less than 100 millimeters annually.
 
• **Rajasthan** is also a dry region, with an average annual rainfall varying significantly across the state but generally low, especially in the western parts.
 
• The monsoon winds play a crucial role in determining the rainfall patterns across different regions of India.

questions.question: In case the President is satisfied with the Governor’s report, he may declare President’s Rule under Article 356 but such proclamation is initially for a period of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**six months**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Six months** is the initial period for which the President's Rule can be proclaimed under Article 356.
 
• The President's Rule can be extended for a maximum of three years with the approval of both houses of Parliament every six months.
 
• This provision enables the central government to take over the administration of a state in case of failure of the constitutional machinery.
 
• During President's Rule, the Governor administers the state in the name of the President and the legislative assembly is either dissolved or remains in suspended animation.
 
• This mechanism is meant to ensure that governance in a state is carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 356** of the Indian Constitution allows for the imposition of President's Rule in a state if the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of the state or otherwise, is satisfied that the governance in the state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• Such proclamations are subject to judicial review, and the Supreme Court of India has the power to strike down a proclamation if it is found to be mala fide or based on irrelevant grounds.
 
• The imposition of President's Rule has been a subject of political controversy and judicial scrutiny in India.
 
• Several landmark judgments, such as the SR Bommai case, have laid down guidelines for the imposition of President's Rule to prevent its misuse.
 
• President's Rule has been imposed in various states numerous times since the adoption of the Constitution, often in situations of political instability, breakdown of law and order, or failure of the state government to comply with constitutional provisions.

questions.question: In which of the following schedules of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the most common wild cat in India 'Felis chaus' listed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Schedule II**__

__
 
• **Felis chaus**, commonly known as the Jungle Cat, is listed in **Schedule II** of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
 
• This schedule offers a higher level of protection to the species compared to Schedule III and IV.
 
• Under Schedule II, animals are accorded protection from hunting and trade, and their habitats are protected from destruction.
 
• The inclusion of species in Schedule II reflects the need for stricter conservation measures due to their vulnerability or declining population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** is a comprehensive legislation enacted for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants.
 
• It provides for the establishment of a network of protected areas including National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
 
• The Act is divided into six schedules, each providing varying degrees of protection to different species.
 
• Violations of the Act, especially concerning species listed in Schedule I and II, attract stringent penalties, including imprisonment and fines.
 
• The Act has been amended multiple times to strengthen wildlife conservation efforts in India.

questions.question: Eutrophication can be defined as:

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an grassland ecosystem
the gradual decrease in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in desert areas
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake.
 
• This process leads to an increase in the growth of algae and aquatic plants, which can deplete the oxygen levels in the water and harm aquatic life.
 
• Eutrophication is typically caused by runoff from agriculture, wastewater, and other nutrient sources entering the water body.
 
• It can result in harmful algal blooms, fish kills, and loss of biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• Management practices such as reducing nutrient runoff and improving wastewater treatment can help mitigate eutrophication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eutrophication** can also occur naturally over long periods, but human activities have accelerated the process significantly.
 
• In severe cases, eutrophication can create "dead zones" where oxygen levels are too low to support most marine life.
 
• Preventative measures include promoting sustainable agricultural practices, using phosphate-free detergents, and protecting wetlands that can filter nutrients.
 
• Public awareness and education on the impacts of nutrient pollution are crucial in addressing eutrophication.

questions.question: Which of the following is the IUPAC name of m-Dichlorobenzene?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1,3-Dichlorobenzene**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1,3-Dichlorobenzene** is the IUPAC name for m-Dichlorobenzene.
 
• The prefix "m-" stands for "meta-", indicating that the two chlorine atoms are positioned at the 1 and 3 positions on the benzene ring.
 
• This nomenclature follows the IUPAC rules for naming disubstituted benzene compounds, where the positions of the substituents are indicated by numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ortho-** (o-), **meta-** (m-), and **para-** (p-) are terms used to describe the relative positions of substituents on a benzene ring.
 
• In the **ortho-** position, substituents are adjacent (1,2-); in the **meta-** position, they are separated by one carbon (1,3-); and in the **para-** position, they are opposite each other (1,4-).
 
• Understanding these positions is crucial for proper chemical nomenclature and communication in organic chemistry.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote Gulamgiri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiba Phule**__

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule** wrote **Gulamgiri**.
 
• Jyotiba Phule was a prominent social reformer and activist from Maharashtra.
 
• He is known for his efforts towards the eradication of untouchability and the caste system.
 
• Gulamgiri, published in 1873, is one of his most important works, addressing the social injustices faced by the lower castes.
 
• The book is a critique of the caste system and advocates for the rights and education of the oppressed classes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jyotiba Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, is also credited with pioneering women's education in India.
 
• He established the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873, aiming to liberate the marginalized communities from social and religious oppression.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the anti-caste movement in India and inspired future generations of social reformers.
 
• Jyotiba Phule was awarded the title of 'Mahatma' in recognition of his contributions to social reform.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physicists and their contributions/discoveries is INCORRECT?

options.text: Heinrich Rudolf Hertz – Generation of electromagnetic waves
Albert Einstein – Explanation of photoelectric effect
Michael Faraday – Laws of electromagnetic induction
Galileo Galilei – Wave theory of light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galileo Galilei – Wave theory of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galileo Galilei** is incorrectly paired with the **wave theory of light**.
 
• Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer, sometimes described as a polymath. He is known for his contributions to observational astronomy, including the telescopic confirmation of the phases of Venus, the discovery of the four largest satellites of Jupiter, and the observation and analysis of sunspots.
 
• The wave theory of light is primarily attributed to **Christiaan Huygens** in the 17th century and was later expanded by other scientists, including Thomas Young and Augustin-Jean Fresnel.
 
• Galileo's contributions were more focused on mechanics, motion, and astronomy rather than the wave theory of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz** is correctly credited with the generation of electromagnetic waves. He was the first to conclusively prove the existence of electromagnetic waves by generating them in his laboratory.
 
• **Albert Einstein** is correctly known for explaining the photoelectric effect, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.
 
• **Michael Faraday** is accurately associated with the laws of electromagnetic induction, which describe how a magnetic field can interact with an electric circuit to produce an electromotive force (EMF).
 
• The correct pairing for the wave theory of light would be **Christiaan Huygens** or **Thomas Young**.

questions.question: Selling of bonds by the RBI will cause money supply to __________.

options.text: No relationship exists between selling bonds and money supply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Selling of bonds by the RBI** will cause the money supply to **decrease**.
 
• This is because when the RBI sells bonds, it takes money out of circulation, thereby reducing the overall money supply in the economy.
 
• The reduction in money supply can lead to higher interest rates as there is less money available for borrowing.
 
• This is a monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• It also manages the country's main payment systems and works to promote its economic development.
 
• The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The primary objective of the RBI is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• It employs various monetary policy tools, including open market operations, to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• Selling government bonds is one of the open market operations that the RBI uses to control liquidity.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the right of the Advocate General of a state to speak in the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 177**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 177** of the Indian Constitution mentions the right of the Advocate-General of a state to speak in the State Legislature.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated after the month of Ramzan?
questions.solution:

• Fasting during Ramadan is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundational acts of worship and the core beliefs of the Muslim faith.
 
• Muslims fast from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib), abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs to purify the soul and practice self-discipline.
 
• Eid ul Fitr is a time for Muslims to give Zakat al-Fitr (charity in the form of food) to the needy, ensuring that all Muslims can enjoy the festivities.
 
• The celebration of Eid ul Fitr varies around the world, but common practices include communal prayers, feasting, visiting friends and family, and exchanging gifts.

questions.question: In which of the following ways were farmers encouraged to begin to use high yielding variety seeds?

options.text: Agricultural labourers were paid wages directly by the government.
Farmers’ children were given free education in government colleges and universities.
Farmers were given monetary support in cash to cultivate food grains.
The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Farmers were encouraged to use high yielding variety (HYV) seeds by the government providing seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.
 
• This approach was part of the Green Revolution aimed at increasing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security in India.
 
• The provision of subsidized inputs helped farmers to adopt new technologies and improve crop yields.
 
• Such government initiatives played a crucial role in transforming India's agricultural sector and achieving self-sufficiency in food grain production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution in India started in the 1960s and was a major agricultural reform that introduced new farming techniques and high-yielding crop varieties.
 
• In addition to subsidized inputs, the government also invested in infrastructure such as irrigation, rural roads, and agricultural research and extension services.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution led to increased food grain production, particularly in wheat and rice, and helped India transition from a food-deficient to a food-surplus country.
 
• The initiative had a significant impact on rural incomes and livelihoods, although it also led to regional disparities and environmental challenges.

questions.question: Ram Sahay Panday, a ‘Rai’ dancer from Madhya Pradesh was conferred with which of the following awards in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Shri**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ram Sahay Panday**, a renowned 'Rai' dancer from Madhya Pradesh, was honored with the **Padma Shri** award in 2022.
 
• The **Padma Shri** is the fourth highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contributions in various fields, including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• This recognition highlights Panday's significant contributions to the preservation and promotion of the traditional 'Rai' dance form.
 
• The award serves to acknowledge and encourage the dedication and talent of artists like Panday who play a crucial role in keeping India's cultural heritage alive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Padma Awards** are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day and are conferred by the President of India at a ceremonial function held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (for distinguished service of a high order), and **Padma Shri** (for distinguished service in any field).
 
• The awards were instituted in 1954 and have been awarded to many distinguished individuals from various fields over the years.

questions.question: Which river originates from ‘Rakshastal north-western tip’ near Mansarovar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej River**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sutlej River** originates from the north-western tip of Lake Rakshastal near Mansarovar in Tibet.
 
• The Sutlej River is one of the major rivers of the Indus basin and is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• It flows generally west and southwest through the Punjab region, forming part of the boundary between India and Pakistan before merging with the Chenab River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sutlej River is also known as the Red River.
 
• It is an important source of irrigation and hydroelectric power in the region.
 
• The river has a significant cultural and historical importance, being mentioned in ancient Indian texts and associated with various historical events.
 
• It is part of the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan, which governs the use of the waters of the Indus River system.
